title: Potentiometer: Reading Analog Signals
summary: Measure continuous rotary voltages with 10-bit analogRead() and map sensor readings.

steps.title: Sense the Spectrum: Analog Perception
steps.markdownContent:
The physical universe is not merely binary ON or OFF. Temperatures rise and fall smoothly, robot battery charges drain gradually, and steering angles vary continuously. A potentiometer gives your monster robot continuous analog perception, allowing it to sense fine gradients like steering angles, joint positions, and motor throttle.

In this mission, you will wire a 10kΩ rotary potentiometer to Analog Pin A0 and convert raw 10-bit integers into true voltage measurements!

```
5V Power ➔ Carbon Track ➔ Wiper Picks Off Voltage ➔ ATmega328P 10-bit ADC ➔ Integer (0 to 1023)
```

steps.title: Core Concept & Vocabulary: Potentiometers & Voltage Dividers
steps.markdownContent:
A **potentiometer** is a 3-terminal variable resistor with a rotating shaft connected to an internal wiper contact.

### The Voltage Division Principle:
Inside `comp_20`, a horseshoe-shaped carbon track connects Terminal 1 (5V) and Terminal 3 (GND). As the shaft rotates, Center Terminal 2 (Wiper) sweeps across the resistive material, splitting total resistance into two parts ($R_1$ and $R_2$):

$$V_{out} = V_{in} \times \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = 5.0\text{V} \times \text{ratio}$$

Rotate the virtual knob in the cutaway visualizer below to see how the wiper divides voltage between 0.00V and 5.00V!

steps.title: How It Works: 10-Bit ADC Successive Approximation Quantization
steps.markdownContent:
Because digital processors only compute in binary bits, the ATmega328P contains an on-chip **Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC)**.

### 10-Bit Quantization Details:
- **Resolution**: $2^{10} = 1024$ discrete steps (from 0 to 1023).
- **Step Voltage Size**: $\frac{5000\text{ mV}}{1023} \approx 4.8876\text{ mV}$ per ADC count.
- **Formula**: $\text{ADC Count} = \text{round}\left(V_{in} \times \frac{1023}{5.0\text{V}}\right)$
- **Reconstructed Voltage**: $V = \text{count} \times \frac{5.0\text{V}}{1023}$

Use the interactive visualizer below to explore how continuous analog voltages are sliced into 10-bit integer staircase steps!

steps.title: Hardware Mission: Breadboard Potentiometer 3-Pin Wiring
steps.markdownContent:
Examine your 10kΩ Rotary Potentiometer (`comp_20`) and solderless breadboard (`comp_breadboard`):

### 3-Pin Terminal Assignment:
- **Pin 1 (Outer Leg)**: Connects to Uno +5V rail.
- **Pin 2 (Center Wiper)**: Connects to Uno Analog In Pin `A0`.
- **Pin 3 (Outer Leg)**: Connects to Uno Ground (GND) rail.

⚠️ **The Dead Short Trap**: Never connect the center wiper directly to 5V or GND! If the wiper touches GND while an outer leg is on 5V, turning the knob to the end of travel creates a 0-ohm dead short, tripping your computer's USB overcurrent protection!

Inspect and verify wiring configurations in the pinout checker below before powering your physical circuit!

steps.title: Coding Basics: analogRead(A0) & Voltage Conversion Math
steps.markdownContent:
Reading analog signals in Arduino firmware is straightforward:

### Key Rules:
- **No `pinMode()` Required**: Unlike digital pins, Uno analog input pins (`A0`–`A5`) do not require `pinMode()` in `setup()`. The ADC multiplexer hardware automatically configures the pin during conversion.
- **`analogRead(A0)`**: Samples the pin voltage and returns an integer between `0` (for 0.0V) and `1023` (for 5.0V).
- **Conversion Math**: `float voltage = rawValue * (5.0 / 1023.0);` translates the count into true physical Volts.
- **Conversion Time**: An ADC conversion on the Uno takes approximately 100 microseconds (about 10,000 samples per second).

steps.title: Code Walkthrough: Continuous Telemetry Stream
Code Prediction: ADC Midpoints & Reference Voltages
steps.markdownContent:
Make predictions about analog conversion values before testing:

### Prediction 1: Exactly what integer count will analogRead(A0) return when the potentiometer is centered at 2.50 Volts?
*Answer:* $1023 \times \frac{2.5}{5.0} = 511.5 \approx 511$ or $512$.

### Prediction 2: What happens if you connect the potentiometer's outer legs to 3.3V and GND instead of 5V?
*Answer:* When turned fully clockwise to 3.3V, `analogRead()` reads $1023 \times \frac{3.3}{5.0} \approx 675$. The top third of the integer scale (676–1023) will never be reached!

steps.title: Guided Experiment: Sensor Scaling & Moving Average Filter
steps.markdownContent:
Real-world robotics sensors pick up electrical noise from nearby motors and power supplies. What happens when an analog pin is left completely disconnected (**floating input**)?

Because the ATmega328P ADC has an input impedance exceeding 100 MΩ, an unconnected pin acts like an antenna, picking up 60Hz ambient EMI!

In robotics firmware, engineers implement **Exponential Moving Average (EMA)** software filters:
```cpp
smoothedVal = (0.2 * rawVal) + (0.8 * smoothedVal);
```

Test floating inputs, ground references, and digital filtering in the interactive laboratory below!

steps.title: Real-World Robotics: Joint Angles & Throttle Pedals
steps.markdownContent:
Potentiometers and voltage dividers are fundamental components across industrial machines:

- **Robotic Arm Servo Joints**: Precision rotary potentiometers inside robot joints provide closed-loop angular feedback so the controller knows the arm's exact 3D orientation.
- **Electric Vehicle Throttle Pedals**: Dual-redundant rotary potentiometers measure accelerator pedal angle. Redundant tracks ensure that if one wiper wears out, the car safely idles rather than accelerating runaway!
- **Radio Volume & Audio Consoles**: Audio mixing consoles use motorized linear slide potentiometers (faders) to adjust channel gain.

steps.title: Troubleshooting Challenge: Floating Inputs & Dead Short Traps
steps.markdownContent:
Diagnose the top 2 analog input failures:

### Symptom 1: Reading Jumps Wildly Even When Not Touching the Knob
- **Diagnosis**: Floating input! The center wiper wire is plugged into the wrong breadboard row, or a jumper wire is loose.
- **Fix**: Confirm that the yellow wiper jumper wire is in the exact same breadboard tie-point column as Pin 2.

### Symptom 2: Reading Stays Locked at 0 or 1023 and Never Changes
- **Diagnosis**: Both outer pins are plugged into the same power rail (e.g., both into GND or both into 5V), or the wiper pin is bent underneath the pot.
- **Fix**: Inspect the pot underside to ensure all 3 pins entered distinct breadboard rows.

steps.title: Workshop Safety & Breadboard Placement Rules
steps.markdownContent:
Observe these critical breadboard installation guidelines:

1. **Never Insert All 3 Pins Into the Same Breadboard Row**: A breadboard row connects all 5 holes together! Inserting all 3 potentiometer pins into row 10 creates a dead short across 5V and GND!
2. **Gentle Lead Pressure**: Potentiometer pins can bend if forced into tight breadboard holes. Align all 3 pins vertically before applying gentle downward pressure.
3. **Quiescent Current Awareness**: A 10kΩ potentiometer connected between 5V and GND draws only $I = \frac{5\text{V}}{10\text{k}\Omega} = 0.5\text{ mA}$ of continuous power.

steps.title: Final Review & Competencies
steps.markdownContent:
Fantastic progress! In Lesson 06, you gave your monster robot continuous analog senses:

- You distinguished discrete binary states from continuous analog voltages.
- You understood voltage division math: $V_{out} = V_{in} \times \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$.
- You mastered 10-bit ADC quantization ($2^{10} = 1024$ levels, ~4.89 mV per step).
- You wired a 3-pin potentiometer safely, avoiding destructive dead short traps.
- You filtered high-impedance floating noise using moving average algorithms.
